quick: 10 mg once daily in the evening
Use if clearly needed; no established risk
Considered low risk; present in milk
Mild-moderate: no adjustment; caution in severe
No direct interaction; limit if NP symptoms
summary: Montelukast is an oral CysLT1 leukotriene receptor antagonist for chronic asthma prophylaxis, prevention of exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (EIB), and allergic rhinitis. Adults take 10 mg once daily in the evening; it is NOT for acute asthma attacks. A boxed warning highlights serious neuropsychiatric events (agitation, depression, sleep disturbance, suicidal thoughts/behavior), and FDA restricts its allergic rhinitis use to patients with inadequate response or intolerance to other therapies.
indications: Prophylaxis and chronic treatment of asthma in patients 2 years and older
Prevention of exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (EIB) in patients 6 years and older
Relief of seasonal allergic rhinitis (2 yr+) and perennial allergic rhinitis (2 yr+) - reserved for patients with inadequate response or intolerance to alternative therapies

dosage.n: Without regard to food; asthma dosing in evening

dosage.d: 4 mg chewable tablet or oral granules once daily
dosage.n: Granules bioequivalent to chewable; contains phenylalanine
No additional dose within 24 h; not if already on daily montelukast
Safety/efficacy <6 yr not established; have rescue SABA available
Do not double-dose for the two indications

admin: Take asthma dose once daily in the evening, with or without food
For EIB, take a single dose at least 2 hours before exercise; do not repeat within 24 hours
Patients already on daily montelukast should NOT take an extra dose for EIB
Always have a short-acting beta-agonist available for acute symptoms and EIB rescue
Do not use to treat an acute asthma attack
Do not abruptly substitute montelukast for inhaled or oral corticosteroids - taper steroids gradually if reducing
Oral granules may be given directly or mixed with a spoonful of cold/room-temperature soft food (e.g., applesauce); give within 15 minutes
moa: Montelukast is an orally active, selective antagonist of the cysteinyl leukotriene CysLT1 receptor. Cysteinyl leukotrienes (LTC4, LTD4, LTE4), products of arachidonic acid metabolism released from mast cells and eosinophils, bind CysLT1 receptors in airway smooth muscle, macrophages, and other pro-inflammatory cells, producing airway edema, bronchoconstriction, and inflammation in asthma and nasal symptoms in allergic rhinitis. Montelukast binds CysLT1 with high affinity and selectivity and inhibits the physiologic actions of LTD4 without agonist activity, reducing leukotriene-mediated bronchoconstriction and inflammation.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to montelukast or any component of the product
relative: Allergic rhinitis where alternative therapies are adequate (benefits may not outweigh NP risk)
Phenylketonuria - 4 mg and 5 mg chewable tablets contain phenylalanine (aspartame)
monitor: BOXED WARNING: serious neuropsychiatric events - monitor for agitation, aggression, depression, sleep disturbance, suicidal thoughts/behavior; discontinue immediately and contact provider if they occur
Eosinophilia/vasculitis features suggesting Churg-Strauss syndrome, especially during oral corticosteroid taper
Worsening asthma control or need for increasing rescue inhaler use
Do not rely on montelukast to treat acute bronchospasm

preg: Available data from cohort studies over decades have not established a drug-associated risk of major birth defects; animal studies showed no adverse developmental effects at ~100-110x human exposure. Use if clearly needed - poorly controlled asthma itself increases maternal/fetal risk (preeclampsia, prematurity, low birth weight).
lact: Montelukast is present in human milk. Available data do not suggest a significant risk of adverse effects in breastfed infants; effects on milk production are unknown. Weigh maternal need against benefits of breastfeeding; generally considered low risk.
renal: No dose adjustment needed. Montelukast and its metabolites are excreted almost exclusively via the bile (<0.2% in urine); it is not known whether it is removed by dialysis.
hepatic: No dose adjustment for mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment, though patients with cirrhosis show ~41% higher AUC and slightly prolonged elimination. Insufficient data in severe hepatic impairment - use with caution.

major: No clinically significant major interactions established at therapeutic doses
moderate: Potent CYP enzyme inducers (phenobarbital, rifampin) - may reduce montelukast exposure (CYP3A4/2C8/2C9 metabolism); monitor asthma control
minor: Gemfibrozil (CYP2C8 inhibitor) - increases montelukast exposure but no dose adjustment recommended
No adjustment needed with theophylline, prednisone/prednisolone, oral contraceptives, digoxin, warfarin, terfenadine, itraconazole
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to food; high-fat meal slightly lowers chewable bioavailability but not clinically significant.
interactions.alcohol: No direct pharmacokinetic interaction; limit alcohol if neuropsychiatric symptoms (mood changes, sleep disturbance) emerge.
interactions.diagnostics: May reduce peripheral blood eosinophil counts; no specific diagnostic interference requiring discontinuation.

serious: Serious neuropsychiatric events - agitation, aggression, depression, sleep disturbances, suicidal thoughts/behavior (BOXED WARNING)
Churg-Strauss syndrome / systemic eosinophilic vasculitis (often during corticosteroid taper)
emergency: Suicidal thoughts or behavior - seek immediate help and discontinue
Anaphylaxis / severe angioedema with airway compromise
Acute severe asthma exacerbation (montelukast is not a rescue medication)

monitoring: Neuropsychiatric symptoms - mood, behavior, sleep, suicidal ideation (boxed warning) at every visit
Asthma control: symptoms, rescue inhaler use, peak flow / lung function
Signs of Churg-Strauss syndrome (eosinophilia, vasculitic rash, worsening pulmonary symptoms, neuropathy), especially during steroid taper
Allergic rhinitis symptom response and ongoing need for therapy
Liver enzymes if signs/symptoms of hepatic dysfunction arise
counsel: BOXED WARNING: watch for changes in mood or behavior - agitation, depression, trouble sleeping, or thoughts of self-harm; stop the drug and contact your provider immediately if these occur
This medicine prevents symptoms - it will NOT relieve a sudden asthma attack; always keep your rescue (quick-relief) inhaler available
For asthma, take it in the evening every day even when you feel well
For exercise-induced symptoms, take a single dose at least 2 hours before exercise and not more than once in 24 hours
Do not stop your steroid inhaler/tablets suddenly when starting montelukast
If you have phenylketonuria, note the 4 mg and 5 mg chewable tablets contain phenylalanine
Continue avoiding aspirin and NSAIDs if you are aspirin-sensitive
pk: Pharmacodynamic effect within hours; clinical asthma benefit over days
Tmax 3-4 h (10 mg tablet), 2-2.5 h (5 mg chewable), ~2 h (4 mg)
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from moisture and light
pearls: BOXED WARNING for serious neuropsychiatric events - the FDA restricts allergic rhinitis use to patients who fail or cannot tolerate other therapies; weigh benefit vs risk in asthma/EIB
Not a rescue medication - never use for an acute asthma attack; ensure a SABA is available
Once-daily evening dosing for asthma; food does not meaningfully affect efficacy
Useful add-on for aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease and EIB, and as oral alternative when inhaler technique is poor
Watch for Churg-Strauss syndrome when reducing oral corticosteroids
Chewable tablets contain phenylalanine - relevant in phenylketonuria
missed: Take the next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: No specific antidote. Reported overdoses (acute and chronic) up to 1000 mg were generally well tolerated; symptoms may include thirst, somnolence, abdominal pain, headache, and hyperkinesia. Employ usual supportive measures - remove unabsorbed drug from the GI tract, clinically monitor, and give supportive care as needed. It is not known whether montelukast is removed by peritoneal dialysis or hemodialysis.
